strings.name: Anish Kapoor
strings.summary: Born in Mumbai and trained in London, Kapoor uses pigment, cavities, mirrors and immense volumes to alter spatial perception. Early pigment sculptures dissolve objects’ boundaries; Cloud Gate reflects the city and its visitors, while installations such as Marsyas reshape architectural interiors. His work often joins sensory attraction with unease. The 1991 Turner Prize winner continues experimenting in public spaces and museums.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1954–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Explored space and perception through large sculptures, mirrors and color experiments, creating visual-cultural influence across regions through public art.

strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Hornsey College of Art; Chelsea School of Art
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Mirrored sculpture in the city
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Cloud Gate reflects Chicago’s skyline and visitors in curved stainless steel, turning visual distortion into a shared public experience.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Experiments with scale and voids
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Pigment, monumental membranes and dark cavities alter spatial experience, inviting viewers to negotiate between bodily and visual perception.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses his Hayward exhibition
strings.timeline.event-01.text: A filmed interview inside the exhibition explored how new works including All of Nothing alter the gallery and viewers’ perceptions.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Returns to the Hayward Gallery
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Large installations, mirrors and black works engaged the same building that had hosted his 1998 exhibition.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Completes ArcelorMittal Orbit
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Working with engineer Cecil Balmond, he created a spiraling steel structure combining public sculpture and an accessible viewing platform.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Presents Leviathan in Paris
strings.timeline.event-04.text: A monumental inflatable occupied the Grand Palais, surrounding visitors with volume and color in dialogue with the building.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Cloud Gate is first unveiled in Chicago
strings.timeline.event-05.text: The Millennium Park sculpture opened to visitors, reflecting city and audience; surface work and formal dedication followed in 2006.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Presents Marsyas at Tate Modern
strings.timeline.event-06.text: A vast red membrane crossed the Turbine Hall, making sculpture’s interior, exterior and architectural scale questions for the viewer.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Wins the Turner Prize
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Following his British presentation at Venice, the award recognized experiments with color, voids and the boundaries of objects.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Represents Britain at the Venice Biennale
strings.timeline.event-08.text: His sculpture presentation received the Premio Duemila, marking an important international career development.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Moves to Britain to study art
strings.timeline.event-09.text: He left India for Hornsey College of Art in London and later studied at Chelsea, developing his sculptural practice.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Mumbai
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Mumbai, India, he later moved to Britain; life and training across places formed the context for his artistic development.
